name: Tapp Tarock
description: Tapp Tarock (German: Tapp-Tarock), also called Viennese Tappen or Tappen, is a three-player Austrian tarot trick-taking game using the 54-card Industrie und Glück deck. Each player receives 16 cards and 6 form the talon. Players bid (Dreier, Unterer, Oberer, Solo); the declarer may exchange with three talon cards in lower contracts or play alone in Solo. Play is anticlockwise; follow suit or trump; declarer needs 36 card points to win.

content.text: Tapp Tarock (German: Tapp-Tarock), also called Viennese Tappen or Tappen, is a three-player Austrian tarot trick-taking game using the 54-card Industrie und Glück deck. Each player receives 16 cards and 6 form the talon. Players bid (Dreier, Unterer, Oberer, Solo); the declarer may exchange with three talon cards in lower contracts or play alone in Solo. Play is anticlockwise; follow suit or trump; declarer needs 36 card points to win.
Tapp Tarock arose in Austria, possibly in the late 18th century; mentioned in Viennese works by 1806. Oldest rules description dates to 1821.
Three players. Seating and first dealer may be determined by lot.

54-card Industrie und Glück Tarot pack: 22 trumps (Sküs, XXI down to I) and 32 suit cards in four French suits (K, Q, Cavalier, Jack, and four pip cards per suit). Black suits rank K>Q>C>J>10>9>8>7; red suits K>Q>C>J>1>2>3>4.
54-card Austrian Tarock deck, score sheet or chips.

Dealer shuffles and offers cut. Top six cards are placed face down in two crosswise packets of three as the talon. Then 16 cards to each player anticlockwise in packets of four, starting with forehand (to dealer's right). If the cutter knocks, all 16 are dealt in one packet.
